gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch correctly addresses the stated issue: it creates shared request-policy modules under providers/transports/openai_chat/request_policy.py and providers/transports/anthropic_messages/request_policy.py, extracts serialize_tool_result_content to core/anthropic/request_serialization.py, deletes all 11 per-provider request.py modules, renames DeepSeek request.py to compat.py and Gemini request.py to quirks.py, splits NIM request.py into tool_schema.py/request_options.py/retry.py, and updates all provider clients to use the new shared builders. It preserves existing observable behavior per the issue requirements.
base_vs_gold_expectation: On the unmodified base: (1) the new test_provider_request_policy_lives_with_transport_families would fail because old providers/*/request.py files exist and new request_policy.py files don't, (2) updated test imports (e.g., from providers.gemini.quirks, from providers.nvidia_nim.retry) would fail with ImportError since those modules don't exist, (3) updated mock targets would also fail. With the gold patch applied, all these pass. So the verifier correctly accepts gold and rejects base.
too_narrow_risks: No direct test for serialize_tool_result_content being importable from core.anthropic, despite the issue explicitly requiring this

No tests for providers DeepSeek, Fireworks, Kimi, Mistral, OpenCode, Z.ai, or Codestral — their behavioral correctness after refactoring is not verified (only structural deletion is checked by the import boundary test)
The Z.ai extra_body rejection behavior (issue: 'Z.ai must continue to reject any request extra_body with the error message...') is not tested in the eval
No test that the new NativeMessagesRequestPolicy or OpenAIChatRequestPolicy dataclasses are importable from the transport __init__.py packages as required by the issue
No test that Cerebras preserves message name fields while remapping max_tokens (the existing test_cerebras tests verify this but only through mocked build_base_request_body, not end-to-end)
implementation_coupling: test_provider_request_policy_lives_with_transport_families checks for the exact filename 'request_policy.py' — an alternative naming like 'policy.py' or 'request_builder.py' would fail
Mock patch targets are hardcoded to 'providers.transports.openai_chat.request_policy.build_base_request_body' — tied to exact internal module path of the gold implementation

Test imports are coupled to gold-specific module names: providers.gemini.quirks (could be 'gemini_quirks.py'), providers.nvidia_nim.retry (could be 'clone_helpers.py'), providers.nvidia_nim.tool_schema (could be 'nim_schemas.py'), providers.nvidia_nim.request_options (could be 'nim_options.py')
test_nvidia_nim_request.py imports build_nim_request_body aliased as build_request_body — coupled to the gold's specific function name
OpenRouter tests import OpenAIChatRequestPolicy and build_openai_chat_request_body by exact name from gold-specific locations
environment_risks: eval.sh uses 'uv run pytest' which requires a working uv installation and properly resolved Python environment in the Docker image
The test patch is applied at runtime via 'git apply' — if the candidate solution modifies the same test files, patch application could fail with conflicts
mismatches: The issue explicitly requires serialize_tool_result_content to be available from core.anthropic, but no test verifies this import
The issue specifies Z.ai and Kimi extra_body rejection behaviors, but neither provider's tests are included in the eval

The NIM module split (tool_schema.py, request_options.py, retry.py) and renaming choices (quirks.py, compat.py) are gold-patch-specific decisions not prescribed by the issue text, yet the tests enforce these exact names

evidence.detail: Lines 27-30: test checks for exact filename 'request_policy.py' in both transport family directories
Lines 117,129,148-164: Imports coupled to gold-specific module names (retry, tool_schema, request_options, quirks)
Line 48: Only 8 test files run; missing test_deepseek, test_fireworks, test_kimi, test_mistral, test_opencode, test_zai, test_codestral
Lines 9-11: Issue requires specific helpers remain importable and specific provider behaviors preserved, but many are not directly tested
Base repo has all 11 providers/*/request.py files present — confirms base would fail the new import boundary test

summary: The gold patch correctly implements the prescribed refactoring, and the verifier would pass the gold and reject the base. However, the tests are significantly coupled to the gold implementation's specific file/function naming choices (request_policy.py, quirks.py, compat.py, retry.py, tool_schema.py, request_options.py) — names that are not mandated by the issue text. This means reasonable alternative implementations achieving the same architectural goals would be rejected. Additionally, several issue requirements lack direct test coverage: serialize_tool_result_content importability from core.anthropic, Z.ai/Kimi extra_body rejection, and behavioral correctness of 7 providers whose tests are not included in the eval. The import boundary test provides structural coverage but not behavioral coverage for these providers.
